project: WO-C2 — Add asynchronous you work watch transition streaming
description: Add `you work watch [--session S] [--follow]` as a read-only, event-driven CLI command over the canonical Factory Event stream. It emits one stable `you.work.watch.v1` NDJSON line per Work state transition in canonical sequence order, defaults to stopping when the selected session's observed Work cohort is terminal, follows indefinitely when requested, cancels promptly, and reconnects from the last accepted cursor without duplicates or polling. The intent is to replace operator-authored `you work list` sleep loops with one composable terminal-wait command while preserving Factory Sessions and Recordings ownership.

context.customerAsk: Build `you work watch [--session S] [--follow]` on the canonical Factory Event/response stream rather than polling, with session selection, finite and follow modes, stable line-oriented output, cancellation, and reconnect/error behavior. Add focused CLI parsing/rendering and reducer tests plus `go test ./tests/functional/work/... -run TestWorkWatchFollowsStateTransitionsUntilTerminal -count=1`, proving submitted Work reaches terminal in one CLI call with no sleep or polling loop.
context.problem: Operators repeatedly call `you work list` and parse snapshots to learn when Work changes state. This adds latency and load, can miss intermediate transitions, and leaves ordering, duplicate avoidance, terminal stopping, cancellation, and reconnect behavior to fragile shell code even though the factory already has a canonical event stream.
context.solution: Extend the generated Work CLI family with a typed watch operation backed by the existing Factory Session canonical Factory Event stream. Reduce retained history and live events in canonical sequence order, project only `WORK_STATE_CHANGE` events into a fixed NDJSON schema, derive terminal completion from authoritative Work-state metadata, suppress replay overlap, reconnect from the last accepted cursor, and expose deterministic finite, follow, cancellation, and error outcomes without adding storage, polling, or webhooks.

acceptanceCriteria: AC-1: `you work watch [--session S] [--follow]` is a registered public Work command; omitted `--session` selects the default compatibility Factory Session and an explicit value selects exactly that live session.
AC-2: Watch consumes the canonical Factory Event stream and never calls Work list/snapshot endpoints, sleeps between reads, or implements repeated unary requests as polling disguised as watch.

AC-3: Every stdout line is one complete `you.work.watch.v1` JSON object with required fields `schemaVersion`, `sessionId`, `eventId`, `sequence`, `eventTime`, `workId`, `workTypeName`, `fromState`, `toState`, `source`, and `terminal`; optional `triggerWorkId` and `reason` are omitted when absent, and diagnostics never contaminate stdout.

AC-4: Lines preserve strictly increasing canonical Factory Event `context.sequence` order across retained history, live delivery, and reconnect; replay overlap is emitted exactly once and conflicting or non-monotonic input fails explicitly.

AC-5: Default finite mode flushes the final transition and exits zero when all Work in the selected session's observed cohort is terminal; `--follow` continues after terminal transitions until cancellation, and cancellation closes promptly without a partial JSON line.

AC-6: Retryable disconnects resume from the last accepted event cursor using bounded cancellation-aware retry/backoff without gaps or duplicates; unknown sessions, stale cursors, retention gaps, malformed events, and exhausted retries produce actionable non-zero errors and never fall back to polling.

AC-7: Quality gates pass: Typecheck, lint, focused parsing/rendering/reducer/lifecycle tests, `go test ./tests/functional/work/... -run TestWorkWatchFollowsStateTransitionsUntilTerminal -count=1`, and `make verify-fast`; when authored OpenAPI or CLI contract sources change, the matching canonical contract generation target is run and all generated artifacts are committed and drift-free.

AC-8: The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; an opened, approved, green, or ready-to-merge PR is not complete.

userStories.title: Expose the Work watch command and stable line contract
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a discoverable `you work watch` command with deterministic session selection and output so that I can safely compose it into automation.
acceptanceCriteria: `you work watch [--session S] [--follow]` appears in the generated CLI contract and help, accepts no positional polling/query workaround, defaults to the compatibility session, and routes an explicit `--session` value without normalization ambiguity.

Watch stdout is NDJSON regardless of terminal interactivity: every complete line independently decodes as one object and stdout contains no human header, table, spinner, reconnect diagnostic, or trailing aggregate document.

The line schema has exactly these required fields and meanings: `schemaVersion` = `you.work.watch.v1`; `sessionId`; canonical `eventId`; canonical integer `sequence`; RFC 3339 `eventTime`; `workId`; `workTypeName`; authored `fromState`; authored `toState`; canonical transition `source`; and derived boolean `terminal`. Optional `triggerWorkId` and `reason` are omitted when absent.
Rendering JSON-escapes arbitrary identifiers and reasons and writes a complete line atomically before accepting the next event.
Unknown flags, empty explicit session IDs, invalid mode combinations, and write failures return actionable non-zero errors without emitting a partial transition line.
Focused command parsing and rendering tests prove default/explicit session selection, `--follow`, exact schema, escaping, stdout/stderr separation, and failure behavior.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented and verified the generated you work watch command, default/explicit session parsing, --follow handling, no-positional contract, stable you.work.watch.v1 NDJSON rendering, optional-field omission, escaping, atomic write behavior, stdout/stderr separation, and actionable validation errors. Regenerated CLI family artifacts, published CLI contract staging, command/input identity baselines, and help/tree baselines.

userStories.title: Stream ordered transitions until finite terminal completion
userStories.description: As an operator waiting for a run to finish, I want the default watch mode to report every observed Work transition in order and stop when the selected session's observed Work is terminal so that no external sleep loop is needed.
acceptanceCriteria: The operation subscribes to the selected Factory Session's canonical Factory Event stream and consumes retained history before live delivery; it never uses Work list/snapshot polling as a data or synchronization path.
Only canonical `WORK_STATE_CHANGE` events produce output lines; other events may update required session/definition projection state but do not appear on stdout.

Output follows strictly increasing canonical `context.sequence` order. Repeated event IDs or replay-overlap records at or before the last accepted cursor are ignored exactly once; a different event that reuses or regresses the accepted ordering position returns a classifiable stream-integrity error.
The reducer maintains explicit state for the Work cohort established by canonical retained/live events and uses authoritative Work-state terminal metadata rather than state-name heuristics.

In default finite mode, watch remains attached while any observed cohort member is non-terminal, emits and flushes the final terminal transition, then exits zero when every cohort member is terminal; an already-terminal retained cohort exits without waiting for another live event.

Focused reducer/stream tests prove retained-to-live order, interleaved Work IDs, duplicate avoidance, non-transition filtering, already-terminal behavior, final-line-before-exit behavior, and terminal stopping.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the Work watch operation over the canonical Factory Session Factory Event SSE stream. The reducer consumes retained history and live delivery in canonical context.sequence order, suppresses exact replay duplicates, rejects conflicting event IDs and non-monotonic sequences, projects only WORK_STATE_CHANGE events, tracks an explicit Work cohort, and derives terminal status from Factory WorkState metadata. Finite mode emits the final terminal transition before exiting and handles already-terminal retained cohorts. Added reducer, finite-stream, and real SSE parser/route tests; regenerated Wire and verified focused plus CLI/Work/Wire package tests. Stories 003 and 004 remain for follow/cancellation/reconnect and public end-to-end coverage.

userStories.title: Support follow mode, cancellation, and lossless reconnect
userStories.description: As an operator running a long-lived monitor, I want watch to remain attached, cancel cleanly, and recover transient stream disconnects so that monitoring is reliable without becoming polling.
acceptanceCriteria: With `--follow`, terminal Work transitions are emitted normally but do not terminate watch; later canonical transitions continue until cancellation or an unrecoverable error.

Ctrl-C or parent-context cancellation interrupts blocked reads and reconnect backoff promptly, closes the active stream, never writes a partial JSON line, and returns the established CLI cancellation exit behavior without reporting cancellation as a server fault.

On a retryable transport disconnect, watch performs bounded reconnect attempts with bounded backoff using the last accepted canonical event ID/sequence cursor; retained/live overlap after reconnect produces no duplicate and the next unseen transition remains ordered.

Invalid or stale reconnect cursors, explicit retention gaps, malformed Work transition payloads, unknown sessions, authorization failures, and exhausted retryable failures terminate non-zero with safe, actionable stderr context including the selected session and recovery surface where applicable.
Reconnect never calls a list/snapshot endpoint, starts a storage engine, writes a durable cursor journal, or converts repeated unary requests into a watch substitute.

Focused stream tests use deterministic channels/fakes rather than sleeps to prove follow-after-terminal, cancellation during read and backoff, retry/resume, duplicate suppression, retention-gap failure, malformed-event failure, and exhausted reconnect behavior.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented follow mode over the canonical Factory Event SSE stream, prompt cancellation that closes active reads, bounded cancellation-aware reconnect backoff, after_event_id/after_sequence cursor resume, replay-overlap suppression through the existing reducer, and non-retryable handling for cursor/session/auth/protocol/malformed-event failures. Added deterministic follow, read/backoff cancellation, cursor resume, retention-gap, status classification, malformed-event/transition, retry exhaustion, and HTTP query tests. Focused Work CLI tests, race tests, Wire/CLI/Work package tests, go vet, and diff checks pass. make verify-fast remains environment-blocked by missing Bun types and the existing TypeScript baseUrl deprecation; package-count/boundary gates report unrelated repository baseline debt. Story 004 remains for public end-to-end CLI proof and reference documentation.

userStories.title: Prove terminal observation through the public CLI
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want an end-to-end regression proving Work submission and terminal observation happen in one watch invocation so that the old missing-command and polling-only behavior cannot return.
acceptanceCriteria: `TestWorkWatchFollowsStateTransitionsUntilTerminal` constructs through `root.BuildProcess`, invokes customer-facing CLI flows through `Process.Execute`, submits deterministic Work through supported edges, and starts one `you work watch` invocation for the selected session.

The scenario observes ordered NDJSON transition lines through the terminal transition, verifies the terminal line is last and finite watch exits successfully, and contains no sleep, Work-list polling loop, timeout-padded polling helper, or direct internal-state shortcut.
The regression fails on the prior behavior where `you work watch` is missing and directly proves the customer outcome that submitted Work reaches terminal in one CLI call.

CLI help/reference text documents default session selection, NDJSON fields, ordering, finite versus `--follow` termination, Ctrl-C, reconnect behavior, and representative PowerShell/`jq` consumption without promising durable history.

If public OpenAPI or generated CLI contract sources changed, run the matching canonical generation target (`make generate-api`, scoped interface generation, or the repository CLI-contract generator as applicable) and verify generated artifacts match authored sources; generated files are not hand-edited.
`go test ./tests/functional/work/... -run TestWorkWatchFollowsStateTransitionsUntilTerminal -count=1` passes.
`make verify-fast` passes, and required lint/typecheck/tests are terminal and passing before merge.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the public root.BuildProcess/Process.Execute end-to-end regression with one finite you work watch invocation, deterministic public Work submission and move transitions, ordered you.work.watch.v1 NDJSON assertions, terminal-last/successful completion checks, and no sleep/list polling/internal-state shortcut. Added the required CLI reference/help documentation and smoke markers, regenerated CLI contract artifacts, and refreshed the command identity baseline with the supported writer. The exact focused functional test, docs smoke, Work CLI/Wire/command-identity tests, race test, and diff check pass. make verify-fast now completes typecheck, MCP checks, and the full UI suite but remains blocked by the existing unrelated Windows pkg/platform/runtimeartifact mode assertion (0666 observed versus 0600 expected).
